newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian state to pay part of Fortis' ASLK charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian state to pay part of Fortis' ASLK charges.

text.p: The Belgian state will have to pay part of losses incurred on the sale of French real estate by ASLK-CGER Bank, a unit of Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis, ASLK/Fortis said on Thursday.

ASLK, 49.9 percent owned by Fortis, booked a 6.82 billion franc 1996 group profit, up 25 percent despite a 3.06 billion franc extraordinary charge related to the sale of the bank's French real estate portfolio, the bank said at its annual earnings news conference.

When Fortis bought its ASLK stake from the Belgian state in late 1993, it was agreed the state, via state holding company FPM/SFP, would be held responsible for future losses related to French real estate activities.

ASLK's 1996 real estate charge, which follows heavy charges on French real estate in the early nineties, has been fully discounted in ASLK accounts, but half of it will be recuperated from the Belgian state by Fortis.
"The risk on France lies with FPM and will be discounted there," Fortis managing director Valere Croes said in reply to questions at the news conference.
He added that Fortis and FPM would discuss the precise terms of the settlement at a meeting in the coming weeks.
